APRV-277: the AgentMail draft edit is PATCH, and a not-modified 400 stops being reported as a failure

Two corrections found against live systems, one in a runbook and one on the
listener's terminal. Nothing here changes a decision, a log record, or a
gating path.

examples/agentmail-demo.md. Steps 9 and 10 edited the draft with POST on
/v0/inboxes/{inbox}/drafts/{draft}. AgentMail answers not_found for POST on
that path (verified live 2026-09-06); PATCH with the same body works and
returns the updated draft. Both steps now use PATCH, step 10 shows the restore
call rather than describing it, and the doc says what POST does so a reader who
already hit it knows why. Draft ids are UUIDs, so the "dr_..." placeholders at
the export and in the payload snapshot are gone. The grant-untouched promise
in steps 9-10 is left exactly as it stood, and step 10 now states it at the
point where the same token is spent.

src/channels/telegram.ts. call() threw "HTTP <status>" without reading the
error body, so the Bot API's own description was discarded and every failure
read as a bare status. It is read now (best effort, redacted, JSON or not) and
carried on TelegramApiError as `status` and `description`, and the message
quotes it. That makes the reported noise identifiable: Telegram answers 400
"Bad Request: message is not modified" when an edit changes nothing, which is
what re-annotating an already-annotated message is. isMessageNotModified()
names that one case and the four reporting sites (annotate-the-decided, the
digest redraw, annotateQuietly, and the listener's dispatch pass in
src/cli/channel-telegram.ts) print nothing for it. Every other 400 and every
other status still warns, now saying what the Bot API said.

Backlog: this branch's record is APRV-279. APRV-277 was not present on
origin/main at 30e4899.

NOT VERIFIED: the gate stopped answering part-way through this session, so
npm run build, npm test, npm run lint and npm run typecheck were never run.
The code and tests are written and reviewed by reading only.
